note: [agent-bulk] numucc_em, 33 showers. Verdict shower 17067 (pdg 11, kine_charge 252.1, 10 seg) -- the first pdg-11 entry of in_scope. I PASSED OVER the higher-charge in-scope object 17023 (pdg 13, kine_charge 455.2, kine_best 635.7, 276 cm over 2 segments): it is the muon, drawn blue, running from the vertex to the far wall, and it is not an EM shower. The other 31 showers are all sub-20 MeV and I did not look at them. Vertex judged off the vtxz-* frames (60 cm half-span, auto-fired: r95 251.9 cm, so the vtx-* set at 314.8 cm half-span is useless here). It is good: three prongs converge on the star -- the muon 17023, the 30 cm pdg-13 track 17028, and 17067's stem -- and the shower start X sits on it. CLUSTERING: nothing is missing and nothing foreign is swallowed. Membership triple-checked and all three agree: nseg 10 == owner-grouped 10 == cmp_div 10 segments plotted (0.0-34.2 cm, 0.0-45.7 deg). Every non-member near the shower is off-axis: 61060 85.5deg, 55054 141.2, 45044 49.4, 53052 78.5, 60059 71.9, then 54053/56055/57056/58057/52051 at 75-90 deg, 48047 29.3, 47046 49.5, 63063 38.9. The one on-axis-looking grey object, 17028 (pdg 13, unowned, candidate row d=8.1 cm / ang 2.5 deg, site 'in_main_cluster (walk_excl...)'), is NOT under-clustering: that row reports where the segment STARTS, and the segment itself is a 30.1 cm straight track leaving the stem at the 8 cm branch point and running perpendicular to the shower axis (-43.1,-36.9,252.2) -> (-43.8,-65.7,252.1), i.e. pure -y. It is the third vertex prong and is correctly left grey. START/AXIS WRONG is the finding worth the owner's eye here, and it is about the axis, not the clustering: the reco axis is dir15, fixed by the first 15 cm of the chain, and the object then bends ~37 deg over its next 18 cm, so its own far members 17019/17031 land at 33.4 cm / 45.7 deg -- visible on the acceptance plot as an accepted orange square sitting far above the 25 deg pass-1 step, admitted only by cluster connectivity (in_main_cluster walk_add), not by any cone. The alternative reading I could not fully exclude, and the one I would let the owner reverse: that 17067 fuses a diffuse ~15 cm vertex blob with a separate straight 23 cm piece (17018, straightness 0.98) plus its terminal blob, i.e. over-clustered. I rejected it because all three viewpoints (az-055/el+20, az+085/el+20, az-055/el+65) show continuous point cloud through the bend with no gap, the bend is gradual (40 deg then 34 deg across two short segments, not one elbow), and a 16 deg off-axis satellite 62062 is absorbed at 34 cm, which is shower-like rather than track-like. No pi0: the event has no reco pi0 group and no second EM object; the kine_pio_* block names E1 0.1 MeV, which is noise, and is not a pairing -- I offer no pi0 judgement. Verdict is about clustering and silent on PID.
